styleAnswer.evidence: The cabinet is a small, narrow piece with a wooden frame and three shelves of red, yellow and green bottles. Measured density is strong: 21 colours per 16x16 tile, which is at or above the well (20) and the stall (17), and 21 distinct colours, more than the bench, hedge and lamp (11-14). Flat-fill coverage is 0%, so there are no dead areas. Against that, 68% of the dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the outline is mostly a neutral dark line. That is the uniform 'sticker' look, unlike the tinted outlines of the hedge (0%) and the stall (1%). The frame wood reads as only about 3-4 lightness steps, and the bottles have little in-bottle ramp, against about 5-6 steps in the well roof and stall. Texture is some bottle highlights and wood variation, with no grain or per-item shading like the references. Because the outline is mostly neutral and the shading is shallower than the references, I fail it on the 'when in doubt' rule despite the good colour count.
